newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican witch says she followed Salinas' orders.
newsitem.headline: Mexican witch says she followed Salinas' orders.

text.p: A reputed witch has charged that Raul Salinas, the brother of Mexico's ex-President Carlos Salinas, threatened her and ordered her to scatter human bones on his ranch, Mexican newspapers said on Thursday.

The accusations, in a court document, were the latest twist in a legal drama that has befuddled and fascinated Mexicans. Soothsayer Francisca Zetina Chavez, known as "La Paca," reportedly said Raul Salinas threatened to kidnap her daughter if she did not bury the remains on his ranch.
Salinas allegedly made the threats from prison, where he is being held on various charges including murder. La Paca has been jailed along with eight accomplices on grave robbing and other charges.

Mexico City Attorney General Jose Antonio Gonzalez said on Tuesday the man in charge of investigating Salinas on the murder charges paid money to the people suspected of rigging evidence against the ex-president's brother.

He said Pablo Chapa Bezanilla, ex-special prosecutor in the attorney general's office, paid $130,000 in government funds to La Paca two days before the buried body was discovered last October. Another man allegedly involved in the planting of the body also received a cash payment, he said.

When the corpse was discovered in October, officials suggested it belonged to a congressman suspected of taking part in the September 1994 murder of one of the leaders of Mexico's ruling party. Salinas was jailed on charges of masterminding that murder.

But authorities later said the body was not that of the congressman but was a relative of La Paca who was dug up from his grave and re-buried at Salinas' ranch on the outskirts of Mexico City. Salinas has denied responsibility in the murder case. He also faces illicit enrichment charges.
Chapa, until he was fired in December, was in charge of the case against Salinas.
